chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel and the Conduits
chapter_note: The chapter is predominantly a compact piece of cosmological-mechanical teaching: why the celestial wheel does not shear or snag the conduits. Only the opening disciple-question is hagiographic frame; the remainder is core explanation using correspondential analogies (ship through water; bird through air).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct dialogue frame and petition formula: "His disciples say to him" / "our master"; this functions as editorial container for the teaching question rather than the impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The reason that the conduits shall not be cut, for they are not cut, is because they are spiritual. Thus the conduits are like the waters through which ships sail. You shall find the prow that is in position in the front part of the ship divides the waters, casting them back and forth. So, when it parts the waters and that ship opens up the water with its cleaving prow, immediately and without delay the waters mingle with each other again behind the ship; and the path of the ship shall not be discernible in the midst of the waters.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution / compilation frame: "The enlightener says to them:" (Layer 2 marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching is an impersonal mechanism explanation staying within cosmic/physical analogy (spiritual conduits ↔ water that closes behind a ship). The only later element is the speech attribution formula.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as when a bird flies up in the air, for its path is not visible in the air, and in the way of mankind, in the sun within the conduits. They also shall not be tangled up in them, and neither shall you find their path through the air known.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same cosmological-mechanical argument via a second analogy (bird through air). No institutional application, citation formula, or exhortative pivot beyond illustrative "you shall find" language.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wheel. It turns through the conduits and the air. The wheel shall not cut the conduits, nor are the conduits themselves entangled in the wheel.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise closure returning from analogy to the cosmological referent (wheel/conduits), in a purely descriptive explanatory voice (how it works), with no frame or pastoral overlay.
